source.title: On the Memorization Properties of Contrastive Learning
source.authors: Ildus Sadrtdinov; Nadezhda Chirkova; E. Lobacheva

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendices; no garbling or cutoff is evident.
record.tranche_reason: It measures memorization profiles for CIFAR-10 random-label training and compares their dynamics with supervised training, using a different measure from the claim’s training-error and test-error outcomes.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own results for random-label training, but it does not report the training error, test error, or chance-level test performance for that setup. Its profile comparisons are retained as results bearing on V1’s memorization subject; cited claims about prior studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study applies Arpit et al.'s memorization-profile method to compare supervised and random-label training over time. These results test V6's claim that real and random labels are learned differently, although they do not establish the full pattern-before-noise sequence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for image-level profiles averaged across augmentations. The conclusion also emphasizes that fixed image–augmentation pairs vary strongly in difficulty for SimCLR, and suggests studying augmentation ordering.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses CIFAR-10, ResNet-18, and memorization profiles across 30 initializations to compare supervised, random-label, and SimCLR training; it does not reproduce the original training-error and test-error measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The profile comparison changes with whether augmentations are averaged or fixed: fixed augmentations make SimCLR profiles substantially different from the binomial approximation and more similar to supervised profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: SimCLR's image-level memorization profiles resemble random-label profiles, while fixing augmentations makes its profiles resemble supervised profiles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive learning's apparent distribution of example difficulty depends on whether recognition is averaged across augmentations or measured for fixed image–augmentation pairs.

record.peer_reviewed: Presented at the ICML 2021 Workshop on Overparameterization: Pitfalls & Opportunities
record.problems: The study measures memorization profiles rather than training or test error, and does not state test performance for random-label training. The reported profile differences are qualitative in the text, with plots rather than numerical difference estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were reported for the claim’s named outcomes. The paper includes cited prior-work claims about fitting random labels, which are not results from this study and were not extracted.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero error on the complete training set and chance-level test error are not established by the supplied text. The profiles concern a 1,000-image subset.
Time to complete fitting and its dependence on the fraction of corrupted labels. Epochs selected at intermediate recognition thresholds do not establish convergence-time ratios.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training and test error across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.
Whether regularization prevents complete random-label fitting, and whether removing regularization preserves true-label generalization.

Direct evidence that shared real patterns are learned before noisy labels within a partly corrupted dataset. Separate true-label and random-label experiments establish different dynamics without isolating this sequence.

missing.what: Record the supervised-versus-random-label temporal comparison: supervised profiles quickly concentrate near high recognition and then evolve slowly, whereas random-label profiles move upward more uniformly. Both random-label augmentation conditions show similar qualitative behavior.

Record the matched-recognition comparison: supervised profiles have a pronounced S-shape and stronger easy/hard contrast than both random-label conditions at mean recognition thresholds 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Neither binomial-profile deviations nor representation clusters establish zero training error. No failure verdict follows from the absence of reported endpoint errors.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares memorization profiles for random-label training but does not report whether training error reaches zero or near zero, test error, chance-level test performance, or the effect of keeping architecture and hyperparameters unchanged.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Training on CIFAR-10 with random labels and no augmentations; measuring the share of 30 independently initialized networks that correctly recognize each image over epochs.
rows.measure: Difference between the random-label memorization profile and its binomial approximation; the paper says profiles differ from binomial curves in all considered setups.
rows.value: The random-label profile differs from its binomial approximation; profile differences are smaller than for supervised learning.
rows.note: This is a memorization-profile result, not a training-error or test-error measurement. Figure 2 gives example epochs and estimated probabilities; the text does not supply a numerical profile difference.
rows.check: Relink from V1 to V6. The relevant result is the weaker contrast between easy and hard examples under random labels than under supervised learning. Deviation from binomial noise alone does not establish fitting to zero training error.
